newsitem.title: UK: EU mission urges support for Caribbean bananas.
newsitem.headline: EU mission urges support for Caribbean bananas.

text.p: A fact-finding mission of European Union parliamentarians to the Caribbean has urged the EU to appeal a World Trade Organization (WTO) ruling that threatens the area's banana exports to Europe, lobbyists said.
The Caribbean Banana Exporters Association said in a statement that the EU mission had concluded that the area would face "mass poverty" if a WTO ruling were implemented.

The European Commission said on April 30 that it may appeal against the ruling, sought by the United States. A WTO dispute panel found that EU import rules favoured imports from mainly Caribbean countries and violated open trading rules.
The EU says its policy under its Lome Convention aims to help the economic and social development of poor African, Caribbean and Pacific states that depend on banana exports.

The Caribbean Banana Exporters Association said that the fact-finding mission of EU parliamentarians believed that the pursuit of democracy in the Caribbean would be at risk if the WTO ruling were not overturned.

It quoted the British leader of the team, Glenys Kinnock, as saying that the EU "must do all within its considerable powers at the WTO and elsewhere to ensure that the Caribbean banana industry continues to enjoy preferential conditions of access..."
She said these were "essential to their economic survival".
